findings.claim: The Aug-4 Drive router is already a single-model Qwen3.5-4B router and marks the legacy force selector as ignored. Compared with the frozen April Project-Frankenstein router, the Drive copy adds separate history/system context budgeting and a reasoning_content fallback, while retaining stale qwen2.5-3b observability labels in several response/log paths.
findings.implication: Preserve the later context-budget/fallback fixes as recovery deltas, but treat model identity as typed runtime state rather than duplicated literal strings; stale observability labels must become a regression fixture.

findings.claim: writer/sandbox/executor.py is a resource-limited subprocess runner, not a security sandbox: allow_network is stored but never enforced, child processes inherit os.environ, shell=True is used for ulimit setup, and no namespace/seccomp/bwrap/firejail/chroot isolation is present.
findings.implication: ClayCode execution authority must require a real capability boundary independent of timeout/tempdir/resource ceilings. Add adversarial tests for network access, inherited secrets, child processes and filesystem escape.

findings.claim: The March SensitiveActionHandler supports persistent pending-action state and SINGLE/DOUBLE/AUTO_REVERT types, but its own determine_confirmation_level returns SINGLE for everything except display resolution. The Aug-6 Schranke is materially stricter: hard-deny classes, command-position parsing, nested shell/SSH reinspection and command-hash-bound tickets.
findings.implication: Reuse confirmation-state, expiry, rollback and command-binding concepts, but do not inherit the old blanket SINGLE policy or regex syntax as semantic authority.

findings.claim: freigabe requires a real /dev/tty, two fresh typed challenge strings, timing checks, command SHA-256 binding, a delay and a limited validity window; its source explicitly states the purpose is to prevent the AI from approving itself, not to stop a deliberate human.
findings.implication: This is a historical precursor to an out-of-model owner capability grant. Current design should replace behavioral typing heuristics with a verifiable owner-auth/capability token boundary while retaining one-shot command/intent/resource binding and expiry.

findings.claim: A non-executing replay of wache-koenig.pruefen classified benign quoted/path mentions as free, direct delete and nested ssh/bash destructive commands as ticket-required, and formatting/raw-device formatting as hard deny.
findings.implication: Preserve these six cases as historical regression fixtures, but add parser/AST/effect semantics and bypass fuzzing rather than relying on regex coverage.

branch_feedback.harness: Add distinct tests for resource-limited subprocess vs true isolation; inherited env/network/child-process escape; stale model-identity labels; one-shot owner capability binding; nested-shell destructive equivalents; rollback/expiry.
branch_feedback.claycode: Model effect intent/resource/authority separately. Parser expressibility or sandbox execution does not grant capability. Owner grant must be typed, provenance-bound, one-shot/expiring where appropriate and checked by external commit gateway.
branch_feedback.frank: Needle/router/model text may propose actions but must not self-mint owner tickets. Recover Drive context-budget/reasoning fallback deltas separately from safety authority.
branch_feedback.q12_index: AICORE router and writer are exact-recursive closed in this shard; tools/schranke and tools/system_control are exact-recursive closed, while the whole broad tools subtree remains open outside action-boundary scope.

earned_work_reason: Project-Frankenstein safety/authority history already has mapped negative-result credit; this newer Drive lineage sharpens the oracle set but is not independently double-credited.
